title: hardware-aware kernel steering for sparse KV pages and prefill scheduling
creator: Aisha Mukherjee
description:
Problem: As we serve larger numbers of models and longer contexts, KV pages show widely varying access patterns: dense contiguous pages from short-context recent conversations, sparse pages with low occupancy and fragmented token ranges (common for multi-tenant and instruction-heavy sessions), and cold pages that are rarely accessed. A single kernel execution strategy treats all KV reads/writes uniformly and wastes compute and memory bandwidth on sparse workloads. Additionally, prefill and decode scheduling do not account for page-level layout and kernel suitability which leads to suboptimal latency and unnecessary kernel switches on the GPU.

Goal: Build a hardware-aware kernel steering layer and page residency advisor that maps KV pages to the most efficient kernel path at runtime and schedules prefill/decode worklets to minimize end-to-end decode latency and device utilization. The feature should: (1) reduce per-token GPU time for sparse-heavy workloads by 10-25% in representative benchmarks, (2) lower 95th percentile decode latency for mixed-density workloads by 15%, and (3) introduce observable metadata so operators can validate residency/hotness decisions.

Scope: This ticket covers design, simulator, kernel microbenchmarks, runtime prototype in the serving agent, telemetry hooks, and a limited canary rollout. It does NOT include model-architecture changes or persistent on-disk compaction tooling (those are follow-ups).
acceptance_criteria: Runtime exposes per-page 'density' and 'preferred_kernel' annotations in traces and Console; sample dashboards for hit-rate and kernel-switch counts exist
Microbenchmark suite demonstrates kernel A vs B performance across dense/sparse page patterns and on H100/A100 hardware profiles
Eviction/residency simulator predicts expected token-level latency improvement and matches canary results within 10%
Canary on 10% of requests for two internal models shows >=10% GPU time reduction for sparse traffic without regressing median latency for dense traffic
Rollout plan and rollback criteria documented and approved by SRE and Product
design_decisions: Compute a lightweight per-page density score = occupied_slots / page_capacity + recent_access_decay, stored in page metadata (8 bytes) to keep metadata footprint small
Classify pages into 'dense', 'sparse', or 'fragmented' buckets using tunable thresholds; map buckets to kernel variants (vectorized dense kernel vs gather-optimized sparse kernel)
Prefer soft-eviction (mark-for-evict) + opportunistic consolidation for fragmented pages rather than immediate eviction under transient pressure
Schedule prefill worklets to read high-density pages first and group sparse page reads into coalesced gather operations to reduce kernel-launch overhead
Expose kernel-selection decision and page residency as trace fields so Console can compute kernel-switches per request and correlate with latency spikes
tasks: 1) Build a small simulator to replay traces and evaluate different density thresholds and eviction policies (owner: Tomás)
2) Implement per-page metadata schema and lightweight density computation in runtime page allocator (owner: Priya Shah)
3) Add kernel variants in runtime with unified API (dense vs gather-optimized) and microbench harness (owner: GPU infra)
4) Integrate scheduler that chooses kernel variant at prefill time and coalesces sparse reads (owner: Tomás)
5) Add telemetry: traces, metrics, Console dashboard for per-page hit-rate and kernel switch counts (owner: Observability)
6) Run microbenchmarks on H100/A100 and produce comparatives; tune thresholds (owner: Performance)
7) Canary rollout, observe SLOs and regressions, iterate (owner: SRE + PM)
8) Write runbook and rollback plan (owner: SRE)
9) Postmortem + lessons learned after canary (owner: Tomás)
comments: 2026-02-16 - Triage: Reviewed by Aisha, Tomás, Priya. Agreed the problem is high-impact; assigned P1. Need a simulator before kernel work to avoid thrashing thresholds.
2026-02-20 - Design sync: Decided to keep per-page metadata compact (8 bytes) to limit memory overhead. Priya will prototype allocator changes in a feature branch.

2026-02-26 - Performance notes: Early microbench shows gather-optimized kernel reduces sparse-page read time by ~28% on H100 for 512-slot pages; dense kernel is still superior for contiguous full pages. Need to tune threshold to avoid oscillation.
2026-02-28 - Security review: SRE requested telemetry redact policy; added requirement to avoid logging page contents and only surface numeric metrics. Added to artifacts.

2026-03-03 - Code review: PR #1234 has implementation of kernel selector API. Feedback: add graceful fallback to default kernel when preferred kernel fails; reduce lock duration in allocator metadata updates.
2026-03-05 - Canary plan: Canary on 'internal-chat-2' model at 10% traffic; monitor kernel-switch rate, GPU utilization, 95th latency. Rollback if 95th latency increases >5% or error rate rises.
2026-03-05 - Next steps: complete simulator validations, finalize thresholds, land PR for metadata and scheduler, then run cross-hardware benchmarks the following week.
notes: Trade-offs considered: adding per-page metadata increases memory but enables accurate steering; aggressive consolidation reduces fragmentation but can introduce CPU overhead and background copy bandwidth. We'll tune background consolidation rate proportional to device idle cycles to avoid interference.
